title: Avoid double comparative
explanation: Better already expresses a comparative meaning; adding more creates a double comparative.

title: Avoid double comparative
explanation: Easier already expresses a comparative meaning; adding more creates a double comparative.

title: Natural adverb with agree
explanation: Agree is normally modified with an adverb such as strongly, completely or totally, not very.

title: Natural adverb with like
explanation: In standard English, really is a natural intensifier for like; very like is not normally used this way.

title: Preposition after according
explanation: The standard expression is according to, not according with.

title: Preposition after responsible
explanation: The standard collocation is responsible for.

title: Preposition after interested
explanation: The standard collocation is interested in.

title: Preposition after depend
explanation: The standard collocation is depend on, including depends on in the third-person singular.

title: Preposition after different
explanation: Different is normally followed by from in standard English.

title: Preposition after married
explanation: The standard expression for a spouse relationship is married to someone.

title: Verb pattern: ask + person
explanation: Ask normally takes the person as a direct object: ask me, ask her, ask the manager.

title: Say vs tell
explanation: Tell normally takes a person directly: tell me. Say is usually followed by the words said or by to + person.

title: Preposition after listen
explanation: Listen normally takes to before the thing being heard.

title: Preposition after wait
explanation: Wait normally takes for before the person or thing that is awaited.

title: Collocation: make a mistake
explanation: The standard collocation is make a mistake, not do a mistake.

title: Verb pattern: explain + to
explanation: Explain normally uses to before the person: explain the process to me.

title: Mention takes an object directly
explanation: Mention normally takes its object directly: mention the issue, not mention about the issue.

title: Avoid redundant back
explanation: Return already includes the idea of going back, so back is usually unnecessary.

title: Noun vs adjective
explanation: Beauty is a noun; beautiful is the adjective needed after very.
